basic_information.short_title: Bangsamoro Mujahideen Under Special Circumstance Act of 2024
basic_information.official_title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE TO BANGSAMORO MUJAHIDEEN AND CREATING THE OFFICE OF THE BANGSAMORO MUJAHIDEEN UNDER SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCE, DEFINING ITS BASIC ORGANIZATIONAL STRUCTURE, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
signed_by: Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: 15 days after publication in the Official Gazette or a newspaper of regional circulation in the BARMM

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Pays a lifetime pension of ₱7,000 a month to elderly or permanently disabled MILF and MNLF fighters who took part in the Bangsamoro struggle for at least 20 years and are poor, and creates an office inside the Office of the Chief Minister to run it.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: The act's policy section states the Bangsamoro Government's aim of ensuring every Bangsamoro is provided basic necessities and equal opportunities, with economic mechanisms tailored to its people's needs. It addresses combatants who gave two decades to the struggle and reached old age or permanent disability without income.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: A qualified Mujahideen receives ₱7,000 a month for life — paid as a single ₱84,000 lump sum in the first year of implementation, then quarterly thereafter. A dedicated office, the OBMUSC, validates claimants, keeps the register, and must review whether ₱7,000 is still enough every 3 years.
who_will_be_affected: Male and female members of the MILF and the MNLF who are senior citizens and/or have a permanent partial or total disability
…who meaningfully participated in the struggle for Bangsamoro self-determination between 1969 and 2014, for at least 20 years
…and who are underprivileged: annual income of not more than ₱250,000
The Central Committees of the MILF and the MNLF, which supply the list of qualified and validated beneficiaries
Bangsamoro taxpayers — ₱500 million was appropriated for initial implementation
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: In force. It took effect 15 days after publication in the Official Gazette or a newspaper of regional circulation.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW. If you fought with the MILF or MNLF for at least 20 years between 1969 and 2014, are now a senior citizen or permanently disabled, and earn no more than ₱250,000 a year, you are entitled to ₱7,000 a month for life.
in_practice: ₱7,000 per month, for life, and it cannot be transferred to anyone else
First year: paid as one lump sum of ₱84,000 covering the whole year
If you qualify as both a senior citizen and as permanently disabled, you are counted under one of the two — the allowance is not doubled
The amount must be reviewed against the cost of living every 3 years

for_specific_groups.Elderly former combatants: Qualify on age plus 20 years' meaningful participation plus the income ceiling.
for_specific_groups.Permanently disabled former combatants: The act lists what counts. Partial: loss of use of any finger, one arm, one foot, any toe, one hand, one leg, one or both ears, hearing in one or both ears, or sight in one eye. Total: blindness in both eyes, loss of two limbs at or above the ankle or wrists, permanent paralysis of two limbs, or brain injury causing incurable incapacity. The office may approve other cases.
for_specific_groups.Women who fought: The act says male and female members expressly — it is not limited to men.
for_specific_groups.Families: The pension is non-transferrable, so it does not pass to heirs.
for_specific_groups.Everyone else: No entitlement, but ₱500 million of public money was appropriated to start it.

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: The Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao.
what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: The law is in force. Payment depends on being on the validated register held by the OBMUSC.
what_you_can_do: Check the three tests together: 20 years of meaningful participation between 1969 and 2014, senior citizen or permanent disability, and annual income not over ₱250,000
Get on the list through the Central Committee of the MILF or the MNLF — the act routes validation through them
Approach the Office of the Bangsamoro Mujahideen Under Special Circumstance, a division of the Office of the Chief Minister
Ask for the implementing rules: the act required a technical working group to issue them within 90 days of effectivity
watch_out_for: "Meaningful participation" is defined narrowly — actual combat, logistics, or medical participation.
The 20-year requirement and the 1969–2014 window are strict, and the act does not say how service is proved; that is left to the implementing rules and to the MILF and MNLF central committees.
The pension is non-transferrable and does not pass to survivors.
₱7,000 is fixed in the text; only the three-yearly cost-of-living review can raise the question of changing it.

key_terms_explained.Mujahideen Under Special Circumstance: Male and female MILF or MNLF members who are senior citizens and/or have a permanent partial or total disability.
key_terms_explained.Meaningful participation: Actual combat, logistics, or medical participation — as defined by the act.
key_terms_explained.Underprivileged: Annual income of not more than ₱250,000.
key_terms_explained.OBMUSC: Office of the Bangsamoro Mujahideen Under Special Circumstance, a division under the Office of the Chief Minister.
key_terms_explained.IRR: Implementing rules and regulations — the detailed rules that make an act work in practice.

benefits.headline: ₱7,000 a month for life for qualified elderly or permanently disabled MILF and MNLF veterans.

direct_benefits.benefit: Cash allowance of ₱7,000 per month, for life
direct_benefits.amount: ₱7,000/month — ₱84,000 lump sum in the first year, quarterly thereafter
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Validation via the MILF or MNLF Central Committee and the OBMUSC register

direct_benefits.benefit: A standing office to process claims, hold the register and handle availment
direct_benefits.how_to_access: OBMUSC — Processing and Validation, Benefit Availment, and Monitoring Evaluation sections

direct_benefits.benefit: A mandatory review of whether the allowance is still enough, every 3 years

indirect_benefits: Recognition in law of service given during the struggle
A validated register that makes the beneficiary population countable for the first time
limitations: No double allowance for someone who is both a senior citizen and permanently disabled.
The act sets no application deadline, no appeal route, and no penalty for a wrongly refused claim.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed by Parliament on 26 February 2024 and approved by the Chief Minister on 13 March 2024.

for_claimants: Be validated through the MILF or MNLF Central Committee list
Meet the income ceiling of ₱250,000 a year
your_responsibilities.note: The act itself imposes no fee, filing deadline or reporting duty on beneficiaries.

what_is_prohibited: The act defines no prohibited acts and creates no offences.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence, fine or imprisonment.
penalties.note: There is also no stated penalty for a fraudulent claim — the act relies on validation rather than sanction.

where_to_complain.first_stop: Office of the Bangsamoro Mujahideen Under Special Circumstance (OBMUSC)
where_to_complain.oversight: Office of the Chief Minister, which has operational supervision and control over the OBMUSC
where_to_complain.validation_disputes: The Central Committees of the MILF and the MNLF, which supply the validated list
where_to_complain.note: The act creates no appeals procedure of its own.

everyday_scenarios: Ustadz Karim, 68, fought with the MILF from 1980 to 2005 and now farms a small plot earning about ₱90,000 a year. He meets all three tests — age, 20+ years within 1969–2014, and the income ceiling — so he is entitled to ₱7,000 a month for life, starting with an ₱84,000 lump sum.

Bai Amina lost the sight of one eye in the fighting. That is a permanent partial disability under the act, so she can qualify on disability even though she is not yet a senior citizen — if her service and income also qualify.
Hadji Musa is both 70 and permanently disabled. He is counted under one category only: the allowance is ₱7,000, not ₱14,000.
Karim's son cannot inherit the pension when his father dies — the act makes it non-transferrable.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Short title: the “Bangsamoro Mujahideen Under Special Circumstance Act of 2024”.

Section 2 — Creates the Office of the Bangsamoro Mujahideen Under Special Circumstance (OBMUSC) under the operational supervision and control of the Office of the Chief Minister, as one of its component divisions.
Section 3 — Purpose: financial assistance to MILF and MNLF Mujahideen who are senior citizens and/or permanently disabled, and the establishment of the OBMUSC.

Section 5 — Defines meaningful participation (actual combat, logistics, medical), permanent partial disability (loss of use of a finger, arm, foot, toe, hand, leg, one or both ears, hearing, or sight of one eye), permanent total disability (blindness in both eyes, loss of two limbs at or above the ankle or wrists, paralysis of two limbs, brain injury causing incurable incapacity), and underprivileged (annual income not more than ₱250,000).

Section 6 — Qualification: senior citizens, and permanently disabled Mujahideen, who meaningfully participated in the struggle for Bangsamoro self-determination between 1969 and 2014 for at least 20 years and are underprivileged. Someone qualifying under both heads is counted under one for the allowance. Benefits are lifetime and non-transferrable.
Section 7 — Cash allowance of ₱7,000 per month: a lump sum of ₱84,000 for the first year of implementation, then quarterly releases in succeeding fiscal years.
Section 8 — OBMUSC is headed by a Director II, with a Processing and Validation Section, a Benefit Availment Section, and a Monitoring Evaluation Section.
Section 9 — The Director II is appointed by the Interim Chief Minister for a three-year term, without prejudice to reappointment, which is on a yearly basis.

Section 10 — OBMUSC extends assistance, maintains an updated register of qualified beneficiaries, conducts a mandatory cost-of-living review of the allowance every 3 years, and performs other functions under the IRR or as assigned by the Chief Minister.

Section 11 — ₱500,000,000 appropriated for initial implementation upon effectivity; thereafter such sums as needed are included in the annual General Appropriations Act of the Bangsamoro under the Office of the Chief Minister.

Section 12 — The OCM, with the Committee on Social Services and Development, creates a technical working group to issue implementing rules within 90 days of effectivity; the TWG coordinates with the MILF and MNLF Central Committees for the list of qualified and validated beneficiaries.
Section 15 — Takes effect 15 days after publication in the Official Gazette or a newspaper of regional circulation in the BARMM.

citizen_questions.a: Three tests must all be met: you meaningfully participated in the struggle for Bangsamoro self-determination between 1969 and 2014 for at least 20 years; you are a senior citizen and/or have a permanent partial or total disability; and your annual income is not more than ₱250,000.

citizen_questions.q: How much will I receive, and when?
citizen_questions.a: ₱7,000 a month for life. In the first year of implementation it is paid as one lump sum of ₱84,000 covering the whole year; after that it is released quarterly.

citizen_questions.q: What counts as a permanent disability?
citizen_questions.a: Partial: complete and permanent loss of the use of any finger, one arm, one foot, any toe, one hand, one leg, one or both ears, hearing in one or both ears, or sight in one eye. Total: blindness in both eyes, loss of two limbs at or above the ankle or wrists, permanent complete paralysis of two limbs, or brain injury causing incurable incapacity. The office may approve other cases.

citizen_questions.q: I am both elderly and disabled — do I get double?
citizen_questions.a: No. The act says someone falling under both heads is identified under one of the two so far as the amount of the cash allowance is concerned.

citizen_questions.q: Can my family keep receiving it after I die?
citizen_questions.a: No. The benefit is lifetime and non-transferrable.

citizen_questions.q: How do I get on the list?
citizen_questions.a: Validation runs through the Central Committees of the MILF and the MNLF, which supply the list of qualified and validated beneficiaries to the technical working group, and through the OBMUSC's Processing and Validation Section.

citizen_questions.q: Where does the money come from?
citizen_questions.a: ₱500 million was appropriated for initial implementation, and continuing costs are carried in the annual General Appropriations Act of the Bangsamoro under the Office of the Chief Minister.
